chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Suleiman ibn 'Amr al-Nakha'i, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever is struck with a bereavement, let him recall his bereavement with that of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), for it is among the greatest of the calamities.

key_terms.مُصَاب: The one who suffers the loss / The bereaved

ai.seo_question: How does remembering the Prophet's grief help in coping with personal loss?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) instructs believers to recall the Prophet’s grief as the paramount calamity, a practice rooted in the Shia tradition of using the Ahl al-Bayt’s suffering as a spiritual anchor for patience (sabr). This guidance elevates personal mourning by linking it to the cosmic tragedy of the Prophet, thereby transforming individual loss into a shared, sacred experience that deepens one’s connection to divine mercy and the Imams’ legacy.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Suleyman Bin Amro and Al Nakhai’e, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who is hit with a bereavement, so let him recall his bereavement with that of the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, for it is the greatest of the bereavements’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Sulayman ibn ‘Amr al-Nakha’i who has said the following: “Abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that if one experiences grief and sorrow due to someone’s death, he should compare this with that which one has experienced due to the death of the Holy Prophet.”
